description: Casos clínicos de lectura de escáneres (Casos 1 al 7)
rules: Traducir SOLO los valores de texto al español, con un tono formal, médico, riguroso y pedagógico.
NO traducir identificadores, claves de objetos, ids de modalidad, nombres de archivo ni tags de código.
Conservar siglas técnicas e imagenológicas intactas (MRI, CT, PET, SPECT, fMRI, EEG, MEG, T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, ADC, BOLD, 3T, TR, TE, TI).
Conservar unidades de medida, cifras numéricas y marcadores de evidencia exactamente en su formato original.
El nombre de la marca 'Neuro Lightbox' no se traduce.
Devolver EXCLUSIVAMENTE el objeto JSON con las mismas claves y los valores traducidos al español.

glossary.SPECT: SPECT (Tomografía por emisión de fotón único)
glossary.BOLD: BOLD (dependiente del nivel de oxigenación sanguínea)

items.case_1.hx: 72-year-old woman. Sudden weakness of the right arm and face and difficulty finding words. Last seen well 2 hours ago.
items.case_1.report: Non-contrast CT: loss of grey–white differentiation in the left insula and lentiform nucleus with sulcal effacement, and a hyperdense left MCA. No haemorrhage. CTA: occlusion of the left M1 segment.
case_1.teach: Early CT signs of infarction are subtle: insular ribbon loss, a blurred lentiform nucleus, sulcal effacement and a hyperdense artery (the clot).
CT’s first job is to exclude blood, which rules out thrombolysis.
CT angiography looks for a large-vessel occlusion that can be removed by thrombectomy.
items.case_1.dx.0: Acute ischaemic stroke, left MCA territory
items.case_2.hx: 64-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension. Sudden left-sided weakness and headache while gardening; now drowsy.
items.case_2.report: Non-contrast CT: 4 cm hyperdense (≈ 70 HU) haematoma centred on the right putamen with a thin rim of oedema and mild mass effect. CTA: punctate contrast inside the clot (spot sign).
case_2.teach: Fresh blood is bright on CT (60–80 HU) because packed red cells absorb X-rays.
Hypertensive bleeds favour the putamen, thalamus, pons and cerebellum.
A spot sign on CTA predicts that the haematoma will grow.
items.case_3.hx: 45-year-old woman. The worst headache of her life, maximal within a minute, while lifting a box. Vomited; neck stiff.
items.case_3.report: Non-contrast CT: hyperdense blood in the suprasellar cistern and both sylvian fissures; early dilatation of the temporal horns. CTA: anterior communicating artery aneurysm.
case_3.teach: CT within 6 hours of onset detects nearly all aneurysmal SAH; after that, sensitivity falls and lumbar puncture is used.
Blood in the basal cisterns in a star pattern suggests an aneurysm at the circle of Willis.
Watch for hydrocephalus early and vasospasm between days 4 and 14.
items.case_3.dx.0: Subarachnoid haemorrhage from a ruptured aneurysm
items.case_4.hx: 81-year-old man on an anticoagulant. Fell at home two days ago; now increasingly confused and drowsy.
items.case_4.report: Non-contrast CT: crescent-shaped hyperdense collection over the left convexity that crosses the coronal suture, effacing the sulci beneath it.
case_4.teach: Subdural blood spreads along the convexity as a crescent and crosses sutures, but not the midline falx.
Extradural blood is lens-shaped and stops at sutures.
Older brains shrink, stretching the bridging veins; anticoagulants make small tears bleed.
items.case_5.hx: 19-year-old struck on the left side of the head by a cricket ball. Brief loss of consciousness, then talking normally. Three hours later: severe headache and vomiting.
items.case_5.report: Non-contrast CT: biconvex hyperdense collection over the left temporal lobe, limited by the sutures, under scalp swelling. Bone window: linear fracture of the left temporal squama.
case_5.teach: The classic story is a lucid interval followed by rapid deterioration.
The fracture tears the middle meningeal artery; arterial pressure strips the dura off the skull.
A neurosurgical emergency: evacuation is often lifesaving.
items.case_5.dx.0: Extradural haematoma with a temporal bone fracture
items.case_6.hx: 58-year-old man. Six weeks of personality change and morning headaches; one generalised seizure.
items.case_6.report: MRI: right frontal mass with thick, irregular ring enhancement around a necrotic centre. Extensive FLAIR signal spreading through the white matter. The necrotic centre does not restrict diffusion.
case_6.teach: Thick, nodular ring enhancement with necrosis is typical of high-grade glioma.
Tumour cells infiltrate beyond the enhancing edge along white-matter tracts.
Pus restricts diffusion, but tumour necrosis does not: DWI separates abscess from glioma.
items.case_7.hx: 34-year-old with a recent dental infection. Ten days of headache and fever; now clumsy with the right hand.
items.case_7.report: MRI: left parietal ring-enhancing lesion with a thin, smooth wall that is thinnest on the ventricular side. The centre restricts diffusion strongly.
case_7.teach: A thin, smooth ring, thinner on the side facing the ventricle, favours abscess.
Bright DWI centre = viscous pus. This is the key test against necrotic tumour.
Spectroscopy can show amino acids, acetate and succinate from bacterial metabolism.
